text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Latest opposition protests in Belgrade brings out 150,000 people. Student and opposition protests continue in major towns throughout Serbia.
- Belgrade District Court judges distance themselves from annulment of local election results by First Belgrade Municipal court, demand access to disputed court decisions.
- Trade between Slovenia and Yugoslavia in first nine months of the year worth 171 million German marks.
- The National Bank of Yugoslavia's decision to reschedule debts of large banks is seem by some as a logical move, while others say it is another means to artificially keep insolvent banks alive.
- Opposition coalition Zajedno says it will appeal to the Supreme Court of Serbia for extraordinary re-examination of the First District court's rejection of its appeal.
- Zajedno claims 50 demonstrators have been arrested in Belgrade so far.
- Nasa Borba unofficially learns that Serbian Information Minister Aleksandar Tijanic is about to resign due to the regime's pressure on independent media.

- Federal transport and communications ministry says ban of independent Radio B-92 not within its competences. Radio Television Serbia director Dragljub Milanovic says reasons for interruption of B-92 broadcasts must be established.
- Serbian government abolishes electricity consumption quotas.
- Private enterprise in Serbia - only 10 percent of private firms involved in production. Trade more profitable.
- New Yugoslav passports from March 1 next year.
- Supreme Court of Serbia acting president Balsa Govedarica says all participants in elections are obliged to accept rules of election procedure.
- Federal agriculture minister Tihomir Vrebalov says funds for sunflower crop purchase will be secured through exports of cooking oil, sugar and other agricultural products.
- The Hague war crimes tribunal investigators in Belgrade to hear testimony from around 40 witnesses of crimes against Serbs in Croatia.
